Permutation City · v3 · A3

Design system

Every token, component and state the workbench and the story page use, in one place. The colours, sizes and spaces come from app/ui/tokens.ts; the components from app/ui/system/components.css, which the app imports as is. Components are built here before they appear in the app.

Theme

Principles

From the brief, section 10.1. Every component below answers to these.

  1. The design never leaves the screen.The map or 3D view is the centre of every step.
  2. One thing at a time.A step shows what it needs; the rest is one click away.
  3. Show, then explain.Every number has a visual next to it.
  4. Colour carries meaning.The meaning never changes between steps.
  5. The machine proposes, the designer decides.Select, keep, lock and breed come first; running is supporting.
  6. Honest about uncertainty.Guessed values and weak data are marked where they appear.
  7. Plain first, with a picture.Anyone new can follow: everyday words on screen, a small diagram for every idea, the technical name one hover away.

Colour

One meaning per colour, defined once. The neutrals change with the theme; the map colours keep their meaning in both.

Neutrals

What things are

The accent marks the selection and nothing else: no buttons, links or headings in orange. Checked for deuteranopia and protanopia in colour.md; every pair and ramp passes, some with a pattern or outline as well as colour.

Ramps

Patterns (colour is never alone)

Forbidden: red hatch. Never built on.
Constrained: thin grey hatch, never a fill.
Green: a stipple in plan, so it reads apart from low buildings.
Existing building: an edge line, quieter than the design.

Space and shape

A 4 px scale, one corner radius, one border weight. Panels are set apart by space and a hairline, not by boxes and shadows.

Layout sizes from the brief: top bar 48, step rail 280, inspector 340, tray 140. The workbench needs 1280 px; panels fold in the order tray, inspector, then the rail to icons.

Icons

Lucide line icons (ISC licence), 16 px at 1.75 stroke. Always with a label or a tooltip.

Diagrams

Small isometric drawings that explain one idea each, before any words do. Drawn by code from the map's colours, so they match the map and follow the theme.

  • One idea per diagram, and at most five labels.
  • The same angle every time (30° isometric), so the ground always reads the same way.
  • Map colours mean what they mean on the map: blue is water, the warm ramp is height, the red hatch is never built.
  • One plain sentence under each. No numbers unless the number is the point.
  • A flat chart where a chart is clearer (the trade-off front). Isometric is for ground and buildings.
Layers

Each map of the site is a layer. Stacked, they show what the land is like in every spot at once.

Rules

Rules sort the ground: some is never built on, some is built with limits, and the rest is free for designs to use.

Landform

Water gathers in the valleys, so they stay open; the ridges between them are where the main streets go.

Streets

Wide main streets carry the city across, routes link the places people go, and narrow local streets make the blocks.

Recipe

Every design grows from a short recipe of settings. Change a setting and a different plan grows on the same ground.

Evolution

Designs breed. The better ones become parents, so each generation tends to do a little better than the last.

Trade-offs

No design is best at everything. The front is the set of designs that no other design beats on both counts.

Massing

On one block, the buildings are given heights and shapes. The sun shows which streets and yards they shade.

Growing in phases

The site is built in phases. What is built stays, and each phase adds to it under its own year's conditions.

What the screen says, and what the code and the papers call it. The technical name stays one hover away.

On screenIn the code and papersOne sentence for the tooltip
Never builtforbiddenGround the design can't use: water, steep hillsides, deep floods.
Built with limitsconstrainedGround that can be built on, lower or greener than elsewhere.

Best trade-offsNSGA-II, NSGA-IIIA search that keeps the designs nothing else beats.

The frontPareto frontThe designs no other design beats on every count.
Kind of designfamily, clusterDesigns that look alike, grouped so you see a few, not hundreds.
How connectedintegration (NAIN)How easily a street is reached from everywhere else.
Grow in phasespiecemeal growthBuild in steps; what is built stays.
What ifshock testTry a design against a flood, a storm or a heatwave.

Motion and copy

Motion only shows change. Words are short and plain.

  • 150 ms for controls (a switch, a chip, a hover); 250 ms for things moving on the map (a design morphing between generations, a layer sliding into the stack, the camera moving to a selection).
  • Reduced motion: every animation stops; changes still happen, at once.
  • Buttons say what they do ("Keep in pen", "Run 15 generations"), and the toast says what happened ("Kept in pen").
  • Errors say what went wrong and what to do next, without apology.
  • Terms get one plain sentence in a tooltip the first time they appear.
  • No em dashes in copy. Text for the author to rewrite carries a COPY: comment in the source.
